payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to suppress electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism. An independent audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold, retracting the earlier 12,000-cycle claim. The battery has a gravimetric energy density of 148 Wh/kg and a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Its operating limit is a 4 °C floor, below which thalliline precipitates from the negative electrolyte and cycling must stop.

The Brennecke Institute originated the thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery, designed to reduce negative-electrolyte crossover. Independent testing established a corrected cycle life of 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee. It delivers 148 Wh/kg gravimetric energy density, with a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. The chemistry has an operating-temperature floor of 4 °C because the thalliline dopant precipitates below that temperature, requiring cycling to stop.
